rationale:
Split into four children, one per conjunct of the conclusion. The parent proof becomes the one-line assembly `fun hVO hREP => ⟨Submission.cmcdt_lpo_tk_mass_support_bound hVO hREP, Submission.cmcdt_lpo_tk_bounded_current, Submission.cmcdt_lpo_tk_boundary_support_subset, Submission.cmcdt_lpo_tk_locality hVO⟩`.

Why the split is genuine. The supplied proof is already four logically independent arguments, and each uses its own subset of the hypotheses:
- MSB (steps 3–6) uses both (VO) and (REP); it is measure theory.
- BC (steps 7–10) uses neither; it is a finite-dimensional norm comparison plus the sequential-continuity criterion.
- SB (step 1) uses neither; it is support topology plus tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω.
- LOC (step 2) uses only (VO).

Each is a standard standalone lemma of Simon Ch. 6 §2 (MSB: 2.7–2.8 with 2.12; BC: 2.1 with 2.4; SB: 2.3 with 2.11; LOC: 2.11; book/chapter-06.txt lines 170–307), and each is reusable on its own.

subproblems.title: Mass–support bound |X(ψ)| ≤ c·M(X) for finite-mass currents (from VO and REP)
subproblems.statement: Assume (VO), the vanishing-off-support antecedent: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with tsupport ω disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0. Assume also (REP), the mass-representation antecedent. Let U be open and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with M_W(T) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U. Then there are a measure μ on ℝ^P and ξ : ℝ^P → MultiVector P n with: μ(Uᶜ) = 0; μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; M_W(T) = μ(W) for every open W; ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable; |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α; T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); and, if also M_W(∂T) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U, μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0. Both are the exact Lean antecedents of the frozen type; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. Conclusion (MSB): let N, k ∈ ℕ, X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) (GeometricCurrentOn univ k) with M(X) = X.mass < ∞, ψ ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) and c ∈ ℝ with |ψ(x)| ≤ c for every x ∈ spt X. Then |X(ψ)| ≤ c · M(X).toReal.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → T.massOn W < ∞) → ∃ (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), μ Uᶜ = 0 ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) ∧ (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = μ W) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ ∧ (∀ (x : Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μ) ∧ ((∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → boundaryMassOn T W < ∞) → ∀ E : Set (Euclid P), μHE[n] E = 0 → μ E = 0)) → ∀ (N k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k) (ψ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k) (c : ℝ), X.mass < ∞ → (∀ x ∈ X.support, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ψ : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) k) x) ≤ c) → |X ψ| ≤ c * X.mass.toReal
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof steps 3–6 (A0: representation of finite-mass currents via (REP) and (VO)). This is Simon Ch. 6, 2.7–2.8 with 2.12 (spt T = spt μ_T), book/chapter-06.txt lines 265–307. Conventions (SimonGMT Chapter06 and the frozen contract): |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α, the Euclidean norm of the values α(e_{I 1}, …, e_{I k}) over strictly increasing I. For X ∈ 𝒟_k(univ) = GeometricCurrentOn univ k and any W, M_W(X) := X.massOn W = sSup {ENNReal.ofReal (X ω) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ k W}, where ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ k W means tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. M(X) := X.mass, which is by definition X.massOn univ. X.zeroRegion is the union of the open W with compact closure (closure W ⊆ univ) on which X vanishes; this set is open (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion), and spt X := X.support = univ \ X.zeroRegion.
1. Fix N, k, X, ψ, c with X.mass < ∞ and |ψ(x)| ≤ c for all x ∈ spt X. For every W ⊆ ℝ^N, X.massOn W ≤ X.massOn univ = X.mass < ∞ (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono, since W ⊆ univ). So the finiteness hypothesis of (REP) holds for P := N, n := k, U := univ (isOpen_univ); its CompactlyContained premise is not even needed.
2. Apply (REP) to X. Only three of its conclusions are used. (a) X.massOn W = μ W for every open W. (b) |ξ x α| ≤ |α| for all x and α. (c) X ω = ∫ ξ x (ω x) dμ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(univ).
3. Total mass. By (a) with W := univ (open), μ univ = X.massOn univ = X.mass < ∞. So μ is a finite measure (IsFiniteMeasure μ), and μ.real univ = (μ univ).toReal = X.mass.toReal (measureReal_def).
4. Concentration. Z := X.zeroRegion is open, so (a) gives μ Z = X.massOn Z. Let ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ k Z, so tsupport ω ⊆ Z. Since spt X = univ \ Z, tsupport ω is disjoint from spt X. (VO) with P := N, n := k, U := univ, S := X then gives X ω = 0, hence ENNReal.ofReal (X ω) = 0. Every element of the set whose supremum defines X.massOn Z is therefore ≤ 0, so X.massOn Z ≤ 0 (sSup_le), i.e. X.massOn Z = 0 (an empty set also has supremum 0). Hence μ Z = 0.
5. The set {x | x ∉ spt X} = {x | x ∉ univ \ Z} is contained in Z, which is μ-null. Hence μ-a.e. x lies in spt X (ae_iff, measure_mono_null).
6. For μ-a.e. x, namely every x ∈ spt X: ‖ξ x (ψ x)‖ = |ξ x (ψ x)| ≤ |ψ(x)| ≤ c, by (b) with α := ψ(x) and the hypothesis on ψ.
7. μ is finite and ‖ξ x (ψ x)‖ ≤ c μ-a.e. So norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const gives ‖∫ ξ x (ψ x) dμ‖ ≤ c · μ.real univ. This lemma needs neither integrability nor a sign condition on c, so c < 0 needs no separate treatment.
8. By (c) with ω := ψ, X ψ = ∫ ξ x (ψ x) dμ. By steps 7 and 3, |X ψ| = ‖∫ ξ x (ψ x) dμ‖ ≤ c · μ.real univ = c · X.mass.toReal. □
proof_key_steps: massOn_mono gives X.massOn W ≤ X.mass < ∞ for every W, so (REP) applies with U := univ and yields μ, ξ.
(REP)(a) with W := univ gives μ univ = X.mass < ∞, so μ is finite and μ.real univ = X.mass.toReal.
Z := X.zeroRegion is open. Each test form admissible for X.massOn Z has tsupport disjoint from spt X, so (VO) gives X.massOn Z = 0 and hence μ Z = 0.
So μ-a.e. x lies in spt X, where |ξ x (ψ x)| ≤ |ψ x| ≤ c.
norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const and (REP)(c) give |X ψ| ≤ c · μ.real univ = c · X.mass.toReal.

subproblems.title: Coefficient-norm-bounded linear functionals are currents with mass ≤ C
subproblems.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ, let T₀ : 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) → ℝ be ℝ-linear (TestFormOn univ k →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ), and let C ∈ ℝ. Suppose that for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) and every c ∈ ℝ with |ω(x)| ≤ c for all x ∈ ℝ^N, |T₀(ω)| ≤ C·c, where |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. Then (BC) there is T ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) (GeometricCurrentOn univ k) with T(ω) = T₀(ω) for every ω and M(T) = T.mass ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (T₀ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (C : ℝ), (∀ (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k) (c : ℝ), (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) k) x) ≤ c) → |T₀ ω| ≤ C * c) → ∃ T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k, (∀ ω, T ω = T₀ ω) ∧ T.mass ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof steps 7–10 (0(b): bounded linear functionals are currents with mass ≤ C). This is Simon Ch. 6, Definition 2.1 with the test-form topology of §1 and the mass 2.4, book/chapter-06.txt lines 170–176 (topology of 𝒟ⁿ(U)), 192–194 (Definition 2.1) and 220–226 (2.4). Conventions. A GeometricCurrentOn univ k is a pair: a linear functional toCurrent on TestFormOn univ k, and continuity' — toCurrent (ω_j) → 0 whenever TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0. TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0 means: there is a compact K ⊆ univ with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j and tsupport 0 ⊆ K, and for every m, iteratedFDeriv ℝ m ω_j → iteratedFDeriv ℝ m 0 uniformly on K. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin k → Fin N} (if StrictMono I then α(e_{I 1}, …, e_{I k})² else 0)), where e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin N) ℝ i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1. ‖α‖ is the operator norm of the continuous alternating map α. T.mass = T.massOn univ = sSup {ENNReal.ofReal (T ω) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ k univ}, and ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ k univ means tsupport ω ⊆ univ and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.
1. Coefficient bound. Let A := √(N^k) ≥ 0. Then |α| ≤ A·‖α‖ for every k-covector α on ℝ^N. Fix I : Fin k → Fin N. ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm gives |α(e_{I 1}, …, e_{I k})| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_i ‖e_{I i}‖ = ‖α‖, since ‖EuclideanSpace.single i 1‖ = 1. So the I-th summand is ≤ ‖α‖² (if StrictMono I it is the square of a number of absolute value ≤ ‖α‖; otherwise it is 0 ≤ ‖α‖²). There are Fintype.card (Fin k → Fin N) = N^k summands (Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_fin). So the sum is ≤ N^k·‖α‖², and |α| ≤ √(N^k·‖α‖²) = √(N^k)·‖α‖ (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt, Real.sqrt_mul, Real.sqrt_sq).
2. Sign of C. Apply the hypothesis to ω := 0 and c := 1. Then |0(x)| = covectorEuclideanNorm 0 = 0 ≤ 1 for all x, so 0 = |T₀ 0| ≤ C·1, i.e. 0 ≤ C.
3. Continuity. Let (ω_j) satisfy TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0, with compact K as in the conventions. Use only the m = 0 part. We have ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ = ‖f x‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero) and iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0 x = 0 (its norm is ‖0 x‖ = 0). Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff then gives: for every δ > 0 there is j₀ with ‖ω_j(x)‖ < δ for all j ≥ j₀ and x ∈ K. If x ∉ K then x ∉ tsupport ω_j, so ω_j(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). Hence for j ≥ j₀, ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ δ for every x ∈ ℝ^N, and by step 1, |ω_j(x)| ≤ A·δ for every x. The hypothesis with c := A·δ gives |T₀(ω_j)| ≤ C·(A·δ) for all j ≥ j₀. Now let ε > 0 and put δ := ε/(C·A + 1), which is > 0 because C·A + 1 ≥ 1 by step 2 and A ≥ 0. Then C·A·δ = C·A·ε/(C·A + 1) < ε, so |T₀(ω_j) − 0| < ε for all j ≥ j₀. Hence T₀(ω_j) → 0 (Metric.tendsto_atTop).
4. Definition of T. T := ⟨T₀, step 3⟩ is a GeometricCurrentOn univ k, and T(ω) = T₀(ω) for every ω by definition.
5. Mass. Let ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ k univ. Then |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, so the hypothesis with c := 1 gives T(ω) = T₀(ω) ≤ |T₀(ω)| ≤ C·1 = C. Hence ENNReal.ofReal (T ω) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal). Taking the supremum (sSup_le), T.mass = T.massOn univ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C. □
proof_key_steps: |α| ≤ √(N^k)·‖α‖: each coordinate value is bounded by ‖α‖ (le_opNorm, unit basis vectors), and there are N^k summands.
ω := 0, c := 1 in the hypothesis gives 0 ≤ C.
TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0 gives sup_x ‖ω_j(x)‖ → 0 (the m = 0 derivative converges uniformly on K, and ω_j = 0 off K), so |T₀(ω_j)| ≤ C·√(N^k)·δ eventually, i.e. T₀(ω_j) → 0.
T := ⟨T₀, continuity⟩ satisfies T ω = T₀ ω, and admissible forms give T ω ≤ |T₀ ω| ≤ C, so T.mass ≤ ofReal C by sSup_le.

subproblems.title: spt ∂X ⊆ spt X
subproblems.statement: For all N, k ∈ ℕ and every X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^N) (GeometricCurrentOn univ (k + 1)), (SB) spt ∂X ⊆ spt X. Here ∂X = X.boundary, (∂X)(ω) = X(dω), and spt S = S.support = univ \ S.zeroRegion.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) (k + 1)), X.boundary.support ⊆ X.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 1 (0(c), (S2)). Simon Ch. 6, 2.3 (∂T(ω) = T(dω)) and 2.11 (support), book/chapter-06.txt lines 215–218 and 296–303. Conventions. For a current S on univ, S.VanishesOn W means S(ω) = 0 for every test form ω on univ with tsupport ω ⊆ W. S.zeroRegion = ⋃₀ {W | IsOpen W ∧ IsCompact (closure W) ∧ closure W ⊆ univ ∧ S.VanishesOn W}, and S.support = univ \ S.zeroRegion. X.boundary ω = X (exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ k ω) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply), and the underlying form of exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ k ω is exteriorDerivative ω.
1. Let x ∈ spt ∂X, i.e. x ∉ (∂X).zeroRegion. We must show x ∉ X.zeroRegion. Suppose instead x ∈ X.zeroRegion. Then there is W with x ∈ W such that W is open, closure W is compact, closure W ⊆ univ, and X.VanishesOn W.
2. ∂X vanishes on W. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^k(univ) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Then (∂X)(ω) = X(dω), and tsupport (dω) = tsupport (exteriorDerivative ω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). Since X vanishes on W, X(dω) = 0, so (∂X)(ω) = 0.
3. The first three conditions on W do not involve the current, so W belongs to the family whose union is (∂X).zeroRegion. Hence x ∈ W ⊆ (∂X).zeroRegion, contradicting step 1. Therefore x ∈ univ \ X.zeroRegion = spt X. □
proof_key_steps: A point outside spt X lies in an open W with compact closure on which X vanishes.
For tsupport ω ⊆ W, ∂X(ω) = X(dω) = 0 because tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W.
So W lies in the union defining (∂X).zeroRegion, and the point is outside spt ∂X.

subproblems.title: Locality: X(η) = X(η′) when η = η′ on an open neighbourhood of spt X (from VO)
subproblems.statement: Assume (VO), the vanishing-off-support antecedent: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with tsupport ω disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0 (the exact frozen Lean antecedent). Then (LOC) for all N, k ∈ ℕ, X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) (GeometricCurrentOn univ k), η, η' ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) and W ⊆ ℝ^N: if W is open, spt X ⊆ W and η(x) = η'(x) for all x ∈ W, then X(η) = X(η').
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → ∀ (N k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k) (η η' : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k) (W : Set (Euclid N)), IsOpen W → X.support ⊆ W → (∀ x ∈ W, (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) k) x = (η' : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) k) x) → X η = X η'
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 2 (0(c), (S3)). Simon Ch. 6, 2.11, book/chapter-06.txt lines 296–303: a current vanishes on test forms supported away from its support.
1. Let ψ := η − η' ∈ 𝒟^k(univ), the difference in the submodule TestFormOn univ k. Its underlying form is x ↦ η(x) − η'(x) (Submodule.coe_sub, Pi.sub_apply).
2. For x ∈ W, ψ(x) = η(x) − η'(x) = 0 by hypothesis. So support ψ = {x | ψ(x) ≠ 0} ⊆ Wᶜ. Since W is open, Wᶜ is closed, so tsupport ψ = closure (support ψ) ⊆ Wᶜ (closure_minimal, IsOpen.isClosed_compl).
3. tsupport ψ ⊆ Wᶜ and spt X ⊆ W, and Wᶜ is disjoint from W. So tsupport ψ is disjoint from spt X (Set.disjoint_of_subset with disjoint_compl_left).
4. Apply (VO) with P := N, n := k, U := univ, S := X, ω := ψ: X(ψ) = 0.
5. X acts through the linear map X.toCurrent, so X(ψ) = X(η) − X(η') (LinearMap.map_sub). Hence X(η) − X(η') = 0, i.e. X(η) = X(η'). □
proof_key_steps: ψ := η − η' vanishes on the open set W, so tsupport ψ ⊆ Wᶜ (Wᶜ is closed).
spt X ⊆ W, so tsupport ψ is disjoint from spt X.
(VO) gives X(ψ) = 0, and linearity gives X(η) = X(η').
